tagline: Develops, manufactures, and sells innovative medical products used in infusion therapy, vascular access, and vital care applications.
hero_kpi_rationale: The consumables segment represents the largest portion of revenue (50% in 2025) and shows steady growth of 6.8%, indicating stable demand for ICU Medical's essential products.

kpis.name: Consumables Revenue
kpis.explanation: Revenue generated from the sale of medical consumables such as IV sets and connectors.
kpis.description: The consumables segment, which includes IV sets and connectors, generated $1,109.2 million in revenue in 2025, an increase of 6.8% compared to the prior year.

kpis.name: Infusion Systems Revenue
kpis.explanation: Revenue from ambulatory, syringe, and large-volume IV pumps.
kpis.description: Infusion systems revenue reached $684.2 million in 2025, marking a 4.9% increase compared to 2024.

kpis.name: Vital Care Revenue
kpis.explanation: Revenue from patient monitoring, temperature management, anesthesia, and respiratory products.
kpis.description: The vital care segment saw revenue decline by 35.9% to $416.1 million in 2025, due to the divestiture of the joint venture in IV solutions completed in May 2025.
kpis.signal: Significant decline in vital care due to equity stake divestiture.

kpis.name: Gross Profit Margin
kpis.explanation: Percentage of revenue remaining after deducting cost of goods sold.
kpis.description: Gross profit margin improved to 37% in 2025, up from 35% in 2024, indicating better cost efficiency or improved pricing.

kpis.name: Operating Income Margin
kpis.explanation: Percentage of revenue remaining after deducting all operating expenses.
kpis.description: Operating income margin doubled to 2% in 2025, compared to 1% in 2024, suggesting improved management of operating costs.

kpis.name: R&D Expenses
kpis.explanation: Percentage of revenue allocated to research and development activities.
kpis.description: R&D expenses remained stable at 4% of total revenue in 2025, reflecting continued commitment to innovation.

kpis.name: Incremental Tariffs
kpis.explanation: Additional costs related to customs tariffs imposed on imports in 2025.
kpis.description: In 2025, the company incurred $33.6 million in incremental tariffs due to U.S. trade policies, of which $7.9 million was capitalized and $25.7 million was recorded as expense.
kpis.signal: Financial impact from trade tensions and U.S. tariffs.

kpis.name: IV Solutions Divestiture
kpis.explanation: Sale of a 60% majority stake in the IV Solutions division to Otsuka Pharmaceutical Factory America, Inc.
kpis.description: In May 2025, ICU Medical finalized the formation of a joint venture and sold a 60% stake in its IV Solutions division to OPF for $211.2 million. The company used $200 million of the proceeds to repay a portion of its long-term debt (Term Loan A).
kpis.signal: Strategic realignment and cash generation for debt repayment.

risks.title: Leverage and Refinancing
risks.summary: The company must manage its debt levels to maintain financial stability and operational flexibility.
risks.score_rationale: The company carries significant debt following acquisitions (Smiths Medical). In October 2025, it refinanced its credit facilities with a $750 million Term Loan A and a $500 million revolving facility. The $200 million repayment in May 2025 slightly reduced exposure, but debt remains substantial and could impact investment capacity.

risks.title: Tariff and Trade Risks
risks.summary: The company is exposed to risks of additional tariff costs and changes in U.S. trade policy.
risks.score_rationale: The majority of revenue comes from products manufactured in Costa Rica and Mexico. In 2025, tariffs cost $33.6 million. A national security investigation (Section 232) on medical imports is ongoing, which could eliminate USMCA exemptions and significantly increase tariffs, especially on products from Mexico.

risks.title: Regulatory Risks
risks.summary: The company must comply with regulations to avoid non-compliance risks and product recalls.
risks.score_rationale: Medical products are subject to strict regulations (FDA). Non-compliance could impact operations and financial results.

risks.title: Currency and Freight Cost Volatility
risks.summary: The company must manage macroeconomic risks related to currency fluctuations and logistics costs.
risks.score_rationale: Exchange rate fluctuations, fuel prices, and logistics costs impact margins and results. The company records foreign exchange impacts on its international revenues.

risks.title: Customer Credit Risks
risks.summary: The company must manage credit risks to maintain financial stability.
risks.score_rationale: The company relies on payments from customers (hospitals, distributors). Payment defaults could impact cash flow.

risks.title: R&D Investment Risks
risks.summary: The company must manage its innovation investments to maintain competitiveness.
risks.score_rationale: The company invests 4% of its revenue in R&D. New products carry risks related to profitability and competition.

risks.title: Product Litigation Risks
risks.summary: The company must manage litigation risks to protect its reputation and stability.
risks.score_rationale: Medical products are exposed to litigation risks. Claims could impact reputation and financial results.

risks.title: Reputation Risks
risks.summary: The company must maintain product quality to preserve customer trust.
risks.score_rationale: Product and service quality are critical to maintaining customer relationships in the medical sector.

ai_positioning.summary: ICU Medical has no significant mentions of artificial intelligence, machine learning, or related technologies in its 10-K filing.
